description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy percentage (y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, spans from 60% to 85% in linear increments of 5%, with gridlines at each 5% interval. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at approximately 64% accuracy at co-occurrence 1 and gradually increases to about 69% at 10⁴. The FT method (blue line with downward-pointing triangles) begins near 65% and rises to roughly 73.5% at 10⁴. The IKE method (red line with upward-pointing triangles) starts at around 67% and reaches approximately 75.5% at 10⁴. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at about 72% and climbs to roughly 80% at 10⁴. The MEMIT method (purple line with circular markers) starts near 71% and increases to approximately 77.5% at 10⁴. The ROME method (green line with square markers) begins at around 74.5% and rises to about 83% at 10⁴. All methods show a positive correlation between co-occurrence number and accuracy, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across the range.
